title: Beyond Decodability: Do Acoustic Factors Drive Predictions in Speech-Based Alzheimer's Assessment?
abstract: arXiv:2610.01846v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Speech-based Alzheimer's disease (AD) assessments increasingly rely on pretrained self-supervised learning (SSL) models that learn acoustic representations directly from raw audio, exposing the model to recording factors. We ask whether such factors are merely encoded in SSL representations or can systematically alter predictions. Using ADReSSo and three large SSL backbones, we apply controlled noise and reverberation interventions to participant-speech-only, non-speech, and full-recording audio. We combine layer-wise linear decoding, input- and representation-space interventions, and geometric alignment analysis to distinguish acoustic decodability from influence on AD prediction. Our results show that controlled acoustic interventions alter AD predictions across all three SSL backbones. translated_title: 超越可解码性：声学因素是否驱动基于语音的阿尔茨海默病评估中的预测？
translated_abstract: 基于语音的阿尔茨海默病（AD）评估越来越依赖预训练自监督学习（SSL）模型，这些模型直接从原始音频中学习声学表示，从而使模型暴露于录音相关因素的影响。我们探究这些声学因素究竟是仅仅被编码在SSL表示中，还是能够系统性地改变预测结果。我们使用ADReSSo数据集和三个大型SSL骨干网络，对仅包含参与者语音、非语音以及完整录音的音频施加受控的噪声和混响干预。我们结合逐层线性解码、输入空间与表示空间干预以及几何对齐分析，以区分声学特征的可解码性与它们对AD预测的实际影响。结果表明，受控声学干预会改变所有三个SSL骨干网络的AD预测结果。噪声虽然在原始数据中并未显示出显著的诊断组间差异，却产生了最强的干预效应。重要的是……
tldr: 该研究发现噪声和混响等声学因素并非仅仅被SSL模型被动编码，而是能够主动改变基于语音的阿尔茨海默病检测模型的预测结果，其中噪声产生了最强的干预效应，揭示了此类评估系统对录音条件的脆弱性。
en_tdlr: Acoustic factors such as noise and reverberation are not merely encoded in SSL representations but can systematically alter Alzheimer's disease predictions across speech-based assessment models, with noise producing the strongest intervention effects despite showing no diagnostic-group differences in original data.
